Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
Assuming a simple directed graph, the worst possible single operation has cost O(|V|), specifically the maximum out-degree of any vertex. The aggregate total cost over all |V| operations is |E|, so the average amortized cost per operation is |E|/|V|.

* (a) The worst single operation costs max_{v∈V} outdeg(v); for a simple directed graph this is at most |V| (or |V|-1 if self-loops are forbidden), and if parallel edges are allowed it can be as large as |E|.
* (b) Aggregate analysis gives total cost Σ_{v∈V} outdeg(v) = |E|, so the amortized average cost over the |V| operations is |E|/|V| = O(|E|/|V|).
